summary: Instagram is where nearly all the audience is: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best performers are short 'X doesn't do what you think' videos about relatable robots and sound-activated gadgets (gyro robot, clap switch, mic, line follower). Generic 'How does X work?' titles on everyday devices (smoke detector, tap, ultrasonic, smartwatch) get very little reach, and recent uploads like DHT11 and the PIR blanket video are underperforming.
winningPattern: Hindi videos about a fun robot or a sound/clap-activated gadget, posted on Instagram. The hook is a surprising claim that flips what people assume ('Clap switch doesn't hear claps, only noise', 'Robot falls instantly without gyro', 'Mic does the opposite of a speaker'). Titles are short, in Hinglish, with one emoji and a clear 'X doesn't do Y, it does Z' contrast. Saves and shares are highest when the video shows a robot or a clap/whistle demo.
doMore: Make robot and clap/sound-trigger videos first, as they consistently get 1,200+ Instagram views, and make follow-ups to the clap switch and gyro robot hits
Use the 'it doesn't do X, it actually does Y' title formula in short Hinglish with one emoji
Post Instagram-first and cross-post to YouTube only with a stronger first-second visual hook
Show a visible demo or a failing/funny moment in the first second (robot tipping over, light switching on from a whistle)
Add a clear call to save or share on the end frame, as IR sensor and clap videos earned the most shares
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' titles on everyday devices like smoke alarms, taps and smartwatches
Uploading to YouTube only, or leaving videos off Instagram (PIR, Phone, Touchscreen, Mall Door, Robot Sunta Hai got zero IG)
Posting English-only videos, since the one English upload got no Instagram reach and little YouTube traction
